title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 86
paragraphs: When the Greeks had buried their dead at Plataea, they at once resolved in common council to march on Thebes and demand that the Thebans surrender those who had taken the side of the Medes — chief among them Timagenides and Attaginos, who were leaders equal to the first; and if the Thebans did not give them up, they resolved not to retire from the city until they had taken it. Having so resolved, they came accordingly on the eleventh day after the battle and began to besiege the Thebans, demanding that the men be handed over. When the Thebans refused, they began to lay waste their land and attack their wall.
